summary.text: A chemical equation is the symbolic representation of a chemical reaction, written with symbols and chemical formulas.
The reactants go on the left and the products on the right, with an arrow that points toward the products to show the direction.
An equation is balanced by choosing coefficients so each side has the same number of atoms of every element.

facts.label: First one drawn
facts.value: Jean Beguin diagrammed the first one in 1615

facts.label: Missing coefficient
facts.value: If no number is written, the coefficient is 1

facts.label: Heat symbol
facts.value: A delta on the arrow shows heat is added

facts.label: Light symbol
facts.value: The expression hν shows energy added as light

facts.label: Simple balancing
facts.value: Simple equations can be balanced by trial and error

items.prompt: In an equation, a formula appears with no number in front of it. How many entities of that substance take part in the reaction?

options.label: Two, the smallest group that can react
Zero, since it is not counted at all
One, since the missing number equals 1
However many the chemist later chooses

items.explain: If the coefficient is not written, it is equal to 1, and the coefficient specifies how many entities are involved.

items.prompt: A textbook equation has a small triangle drawn on its reaction arrow. What does it show?

options.label: Heat is added to the reaction as energy
Light is added to the reaction as energy
The equation has been checked and balanced
The reaction runs in both directions

items.explain: A delta or triangle on the arrow shows that energy in the form of heat is added to the reaction.

items.prompt: A student counts atoms for a reaction. Carbon matches on both sides, but hydrogen shows 4 on the left and 2 on the right. What should she do?

options.label: Accept it, since carbon already matches
Delete the extra hydrogen from the left
Add some new element to the right side
Change coefficients until hydrogen agrees

items.explain: Each side must have the same number of atoms of each element, and an equation is balanced by assigning suitable coefficients.

items.prompt: Why must an equation show the same atoms of each element on both sides?

options.label: Because atoms keep changing into other elements and back again
Because elements pass through a chemical reaction unchanged
Because the arrow works as an equals sign between the two sides
Because plus signs ask you to add up the atoms in each side

items.explain: No nuclear reactions take place in a chemical reaction, so the elements pass through unchanged and each side must show the same number of atoms.

items.prompt: While balancing by trial and error, you reach a coefficient like 1/2. What clears the fraction?

options.label: Scale every coefficient by the lowest common denominator
Round each fraction to the nearest whole number you like
Remove the substance carrying the fraction entirely
Double only the coefficient that holds the fraction

items.explain: Fractions can be eliminated by multiplying all coefficients by their lowest common denominator.

items.prompt: A chemist wants to show that a reaction runs in an acidic medium but does not name a specific acid. What can she write on top of the arrow?

options.label: OH⁻
Δ
H⁺
hν

items.explain: Writing H⁺ (or even "acid") on top of the arrow denotes an acidic medium when no specific acid is required.
